utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated and have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to say good morning to all counsel, and to the interpreters, of course. We can now resume our day's work, starting by having Brigadier Marin brought into the courtroom. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabuddeen and myself received the translation of the document 510. I think there is nothing further to say. The Judges will read it, in view of what was in both those documents, but, of course, you can decide, Mr. Kehoe, at what point you want to go back to Exhibit 510, or if you would like to go on with what we interrupted yesterday. You are the one who has to decide. Was it 510 or 511, Mr. Dubuisson?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's 510, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, 510.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With Your Honours' permission, I would like to go back to this area and complete the inquiry on these documents and then move back to where we left off yesterday, Mr. President. So, if we could, Mr. Dubuisson, please give 510, and the map, 511, to Brigadier Marin. And then if we could also, if we could give Prosecutor's Exhibit 337 and 339 to the Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You were talking about 337 and 339 of the Prosecutor, that's the ones you're talking about; is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it should be photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, turning our attention back to 510, the order of Mijo Bozic on the 27th of January 1993, we have a translation, both in French and English, from the translation section on the first sentence of paragraph 2, which notes that, "After the preparation has been completed, the local population is to be called to surrender unconditionally all weapons, otherwise the village will be burned to the ground. The villages will be burned to the ground." And then on paragraph 3 it reads, "After these villages have been taken, the enemy is to be pushed back toward Bukovci with the aim of crushing and destroying that village and the enemy forces in it. The Bukovci village must be taken by nightfall on condition that we burn anything standing in the way." Now, Brigadier, this operation, according to this order, was to commence at 1600 hours on the 27th of January. Did the Ban Jelacic Brigade burn villages on the way up to Bukovci, as is stated in this order by Mijo Bozic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, to the best of my knowledge, until the present day, the Brigade Ban Jelacic did not carry out these tasks, according to this. That is to say, they did not disarm these villages or burn them down. That is to say, the population was not disarmed and the villages were not burned, as far as I know. Because about this order and about these activities, I received no information in the Operative Zone; but that is what I know until the present day. Something else in this connection: All these villages, that is to say, in the wider region of Bilalovac, on that day were put under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; and during the war, that is to say in 1993, those villages were under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, are you telling us, Brigadier, that you do not know anything about this order? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As concerns this order, I have seen it for the first time, and this was at this Court yesterday when you showed it to me. I thought about it, I tried to remember, and I remembered what I just said. I did not have any information then about this order, but today, that I think about it, and when I know what the situation on the ground was, to the best of my knowledge, these villages were not attacked, were not burned down, and these villages, on the 27th and the 28th were put under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and on those villages the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina held them under their control until the end of the war, that is to say, until the Washington Accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take a look at Exhibit 337 in conjunction with 510; and on 4, the order by Bozic says, "I hereby charge Mr. Mato Lucic, brigade commander, with coordinating this operation and Mr. Marinko Tuka as his deputy. Now, take a look on the ELMO, the photograph on the ELMO, and that photograph has been previously identified as Mato Lucic; do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Mato Lucic, but I cannot recognise him on this photograph. That is to say, I cannot claim that this is him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at Exhibit 339, which is another photograph of Mato Lucic and others; do you recognise Mato Lucic in that photograph, standing in the back behind Blaskic and Rajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that it is the same person as on the other photograph, but truly I cannot claim that I am sure that this is Mato Lucic. I recognise General Blaskic. I recognise, according to the moustache, this should be Rajic; but I cannot claim that this is Mato Lucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. We will move on to that and come back to these photographs and exhibits at a later time. Thank you very much. We're going to change subjects now and go back to where we left off yesterday. If I might have one moment, Mr. President. Now, Brigadier, yesterday we left off with a series of exhibits that talked about the attacks by the Bosnian Serbs on the Bosnian Muslims, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, between February and March and April, that ended with the fall of Srebrenica on the 16th of April 1993, the day of the attacks in the Lasva Valley area. At the same time that the attacks were taking place against the Bosnian Muslims, or the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were negotiations on the Vance-Owen Peace Plan; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that in April the Vance-Owen Plan was a topical affair and that negotiations were held in Geneva about this. So that is the only thing I can say at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at Exhibit 19, Prosecution Exhibit 19, if we could put that on the ELMO. Yes, that's it. Can we pull that up in colour? No?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What you see on the projector is in colour, but we're having technical problems, we can't produce a colour picture on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, we will move ahead without it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, take a look at that, and take a look at it closely, and if you can't see it on the monitor --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the Court's permission if the witness could take the document off the ELMO and look at it up close, because I think it is a little difficult to see on the monitor. Mr. Usher, could you give that exhibit to the witness? I think it's easier to see, in fairness to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Less equitable for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What I suggest is that the Brigadier share it with us. Usher, would you remain standing for a minute and help us here? You take a look at it and then we will be able to look at it, as well. We should have it. I know this is Exhibit 19, it must be in my office. All right, Brigadier, have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, the cantons that are listed here, 3, 8 and 10, are the cantons that were supposed to go to the Bosnian Croats; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of this map, I cannot tell, because the contents of the negotiations that were held in Geneva, I mean, if I had that, we could talk about it. But on the basis of this map and this geography and these colours, I cannot say what was supposed to belong to who. Because the internal set up of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the basis of the Vance-Owen Plan, cannot lend itself to yes, no answers. This entire procedure is involved, and this map speaks of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Answer this simply, Brigadier, otherwise you're going to spend a month here. I could tell you now you're going to spend a month here. You can't say you really were unfamiliar with the Vance-Owen Plan. It's an easy question. For a year that we have been talking about it, in your opinion, did these provinces, referred to by the Prosecutor, that is 3, 8 and 10, did you hear they were supposed to go back to the Bosnian Croats? That's the question, it seems easy to me. If we have to go into a geopolitical analysis of the situation, I can assure you, you are going to be here a month from now and remain available to the Tribunal. We have to be clear. You, yourself, spoke about the Vance-Owen Plan during the direct examination. The question is an easy one, it seems to me. Try to avoid these constant digressions. I'll go back to the rules. It's a simple question Would you repeat the question, Mr. Kehoe? If not, I'm going to ask it myself through the powers that are given to the Tribunal. Did provinces 3, 8 and 10, not according to the map, but according to what you know, that is, according to the Vance-Owen Plan, did they or did they not; or say you don't know anything about the Vance-Owen Plan, but that is going to cast a different light on what you said last week. This is Tuesday morning, it's 10.25, I would like us to go forward. Please ask your question again, very clearly, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, were cantons 3, 8 and 10, as coloured on the map in blue that's before you on Exhibit 19, were those cantons supposed to be controlled by the Bosnian Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I cannot answer whether they would be under this particular control. However, probably, if it is coloured with a certain colour, as far as I know, then the Croats in these municipalities that were included would be a majority. But I don't know in the Vance-Owen Plan whether it was said, whether something would be under someone's control. I understand the Vance-Owen Plan to be an internal set up of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay. The transcript is authoritative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at the map, canton 10 that's coloured in blue, incorporates the Lasva Valley area, down through Busavaca and approximately half of Kiseljak; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does include the municipalities that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention, sir, to Exhibit 25, Prosecutor's Exhibit 25. Yes, that's it. Take a look at that newspaper article, sir, and that is a newspaper article from Slobodna Dalmacija of 4 April 1993. And the article, the heading, the Croatian Defence Council reviewed the documents of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, have you taken a look at it, Brigadier? Have you familiarised yourself with the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have, in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you want a few more moments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please. I have familiarised myself with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, the author of this article is a man by the name of Veso Vegar, from Mostar; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, Veso Vegar is from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time frame he was a member of the HVO; wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Veso Vegar, as far as I know, was in the Ministry of Defence. That is to say, he was either attached to the HVO government for information. I know he was involved in information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was part of the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, part of the HVO, because the HVO had the civilian part of the HVO and the military part of the HVO. That is to say, the ministry, the units, and the main staff, and on the other hand, there were civilian institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular article calls for President Izetbegovic to sign an agreement which would implement the Vance-Owen Peace Plan; isn't that right? And I'm talking about the paragraph that begins prior to the numbers 1 through 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Earlier, further up. What paragraph do you want to show, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The paragraph right before 1 through 6, and carrying it down through the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The one that begins "Until".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, begins "Until" and then the paragraph just below the 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is a French copy of this article. Do we have a French copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to read it, Brigadier? That might be easier, the paragraph beginning "Until full demilitarisation of the republic, the organisation of the armed forces will be organised in conformity with the relevant documents of the Vance-Owen Plan, and pursuant to the joint statement stemming from the agreement between Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic leaders of the Croat and Muslim delegations at the peace talks. The statement was signed by Mate Boban and it reads as follows: "After the Vance-Owen Peace Plan was signed, Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban agreed: 1. All misunderstandings have been avoided between the Croatian and Muslim people concerning the borders of provinces and temporary authority therein and in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 2. All armed forces of the HVO and the police of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as well the BH Army and BH Ministry of the Interior which originate from outside the provinces shall have to identify themselves and leave such provinces within three days. 3. Until the complete demilitarisation of BH as envisaged under the peace plan and for reasons of a more efficient defence against aggression, the domicile armed forces of the HVO and BH Army in provinces 1, 5, and 9 shall be placed under the command of the Main Staff of the BH Army, and in provinces 3, 8, and 10 under the command of the Main Staff of the HVO. Those forces which cannot accept this decision, shall have the possibility to leave the provinces. 4. The Main Staff of the HVO and the Main Staff of the BH Army shall set up a joint command no later than 15 April, 1993. 5. Conflicts between the HVO and the BH Army shall stop at once and never be resumed. 6. The free movement of people and goods on all thoroughfares in the free territory of the above-mentioned provinces shall be made possible at once. The HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna hopes that Izetbegovic, having understood the exceptional importance of the Statement, will sign that document as well, because the document also confirms the desire for peace which is so necessary for everyone." Now, Brigadier, my question is: Three, 8, and 10 were the three cantons that we talked about that were, according to this plan, to come under the main staff of the HVO, and that's in paragraph 3; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says in paragraph 3, but I wish to recall the order that we received from the main staff related precisely to the implementation of these activities which indicated -- or, rather, in which this text, as it stands here, was, so that is what I know about these activities, that such orders were received, that contact should be established with representatives of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The interpreter was not able to follow what you just said easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't know if the interpreter wanted to repeat it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the main -- on number 4, the joint command was not set up by the 15th of April, 1993, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not set up until this date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look back at the next paragraph. It says: "In the event that the Statement is not signed by the heads of the Muslim delegation in provinces 3, 8, and 10, the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has decided to apply the provisions of the Peace Plan, whereby each national armed force will have to withdraw to its domicile province." Do you see that paragraph, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, and that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by the HVO to implement this particular agreement in the Vance-Owen Plan whether the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina agrees or not; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From this article, from this newspaper article, I cannot say that that is what the HVO decided. It says here that that is the decision that was reached, but I have never seen this specific decision. What it says here is exactly what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the command was not set up by the 15th, and this article, written by a member of the HVO, says that the HVO will unilaterally implement this plan, and the attacks in Central Bosnia took place on the 16th; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war in Central Bosnia, in Vitez, took place on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the issue concerning the HVO control of canton 10 continued to be an issue with the HVO after the fighting began on the 16th, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document, this document and the problems defined -- related to the Vance-Owen Plan was probably topical until another fresh peace agreement on Bosnia-Herzegovina was signed, which the top political -- what the politicians discussed at top level, I cannot say and don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, didn't it continue to be a topic in the midst of the fighting in the first few days after the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my role, that is, the role whereof the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia on the 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th, up until the meeting in Zenica, we did not have time, nor did we have the possibility, at least I did not, have an opportunity to talk to anybody on this topic and about this particular issue. What the head of the main staff discussed with the commander of the BH army or the top civilian authority during the time of the war in Vitez, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn our attention to Defence Exhibit 330, if we could? You see Defence Exhibit 330, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it. It is not legible in one portion, but I think I'll be able to find my way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a document that you said you recognised in direct examination by the Defence, and you said that this was a document that came into the HVO headquarters on the 20th of April, 1993. That was your direct testimony. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see the reason why this document should go to the main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, that's what you said. When you introduced this into evidence, you identified it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Objection. Mr. President, the witness did not say that it went to the main staff but to the command of the Operative Zone, and the main staff was in Mostar, and so the terms are different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document that I have before me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There's an ambiguity here, Mr. Kehoe. Let's clarify it. When you recall the witness's statements, you have to recall them very precisely with the transcript in hand. The witness had many things. You've got to put yourself in his place. It's complicated and it's hard for him just to react when you say "You said this." If you have the transcript, you can use it, or else be very specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can pull the transcript, but is this a document that you identified during your direct

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I identified this document and I recall the events that the document writes about.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be a good idea to see whether you are talking about the same document. This is a report from the Vitez Brigade sent to the Operative Zone. Do you have that document in mind, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The document is the report from the Vitez Brigade, 20 April, 1993, to the command of Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Vitez. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document that you identified during your direct testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I said that I recall the contents of this document and that the document came to the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, the last paragraph of this document reads: "On the premises of the Viteska Brigade command, prominent representatives of Muslims gathered during the night with the goal of finding a way to stop the armed conflict. Together with the representatives of the HVO government, certain conclusions were reached, a copy of which is attached herewith." Now, my question for you is: This particular document, when it came in to the command headquarters, had an attachment, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says here. I cannot quite remember what it was. I said that I remember the contents and the activities that are written down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 86, if we could? And, Mr. President, on 86, Prosecutor's, there is a French copy as well. Prosecution 86, it's not Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The registrar is going to give it to me, give me the French translation. He doesn't want me to write any notes down, he doesn't want me to scribble on it. He's right. Eighty-six, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, 86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I promise you I'm going to give it back to you in the shape that you gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, take a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 86. Now, Brigadier, this is also dated the 20th of April, 1993, the same date as this memorandum that you identified, Defence Exhibit 330.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the handwriting, it is 16th of April, 1993 -- 16th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The handwriting on the bottom is the 16th of July, 1995, and the date is in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. The 16th of July written in handwriting and the date has been typed, the 20th of the 4th, 1993, April. That is what it is in my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Take a look at that document, sir -- it's a rather brief document -- if you could.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have looked at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, this is signed on behalf of the Croats by Mayor Ivan Santic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Mr. Santic. I cannot claim that that is his signature because I haven't had occasion to see his documents signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, take a look at point 4 in that document, and before we look at point 4, is this the attachment that was attached to Defence Exhibit 330 that came to the headquarters on the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Well, let's look at paragraph 4. It says: "Both sides agree in Vitez and province 10 the Vance-Owen Plan should be implemented even before it is signed by the Serb side. Also, the army commands shall retain their structure in conformity with the ethnic composition of the province and the municipality."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, sir, this particular document appears to be signed at a time when the war is taking place in the Vitez area; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That means that if the date is correct, the 20th of April, 1993, the 24th, as far as I recall, on that particular evening, there was a meeting in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So based on this particular document, you would agree with me that in the midst of this war, the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan in canton 10 was a significant issue at least to Mayor Santic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the text which has been offered to us here, we can see that it was a significant issue both for Mr. Santic and Mr. Muharem Mujezinovic because they both signed the same text.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about that. During the 19th, 20th, 21st dates down, Muslim prisoners were being kept at the cinema building some 100 yards behind the Hotel Vitez; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that in the cinema building, there were prisoners; that is to say, people were -- Muslims, civilians who, during the fighting, were brought to that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, was Dr. Mujezinovic one of those prisoners, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot either assert or deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let's change subjects now. We finished talking about the Bosnian Serbs attacking the Bosnian Muslims in various categories, and we talked about the Vance-Owen Plan and the decision by the HVO to unilaterally implement the Vance-Owen Plan if not agreed to by the Bosnian Muslims. Let us now move to the actual time frame of the 15th, 16th of April, 1993. Before we get to that, let me talk about a few things before we actually move to the attack. The first thing that I'd like to talk to you about is the actual kidnapping of those officers in Novi Travnik, and you talked about that at some length during your direct examination in response to some questions by Mr. Nobilo. My question for you, Brigadier, is: Isn't it true that as soon as those kidnappings of the HVO officers took place, a joint investigation between the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and ECMM monitors was set up to investigate the kidnappings; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the investigation was set up and the investigation lasted for more than 15 days. I think about 20 days was how long the investigation lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, likewise, for the kidnapping of Commander Totic, an investigation was set up to secure the release of Commander Totic as well, wasn't it, and I'm talking about a joint investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Linked to the investigation, when we're talking about the kidnapping of the commander of the brigade in Zenica, Zivko Totic, I do not have any information. I cannot say -- I don't know anything about that particular investigation. But if you claim that that is so, I have no reason to deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, sir, isn't it so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Pay attention to the witness's answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I did, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think one has to listen to the answers that are given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, isn't it so, Brigadier, that the release of both the HVO officers kidnapped from Travnik as well Commander Totic was tied to the release of some foreign Muslims that had been taken captive and were being held in Kaonik camp or Kaonik military prison camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through the negotiations that were held and after the war was stopped and a cease-fire was established for the conflict in Busovaca, the activities towards the exchange of kidnapped officers from the brigade of Novi Travnik and the Vitez Brigade commander took place, and within the framework of this kind of activity, I cannot tell you any specific facts but I do know that there was an agreement for the exchange of those taken prisoners, taken captive, and I mentioned that in this exchange a certain number of -- I don't know the category of these people. I can't say now who were confined in the military prison in Busovaca. I'm not sure that they were Mujahedeen, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, they were people foreign -- people who were not from Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. For me -- there was this kind of information as regards -- in the communication that I had, and I -- that they were Mujahedeen, but from what country, whether they were foreign nationals, whether they had taken up Bosnian nationality, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, the ECMM and other international organisations assisted to complete this agreement whereby the exchange of the HVO officers and these Muslims that were in the Kaonik camp, they assisted in that agreement, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there was great assistance from the International Community, and without it, there could have been no exchange. But the exchange followed an agreement on the cease-fire and the release of all people that had been taken prisoner, and this was in Zenica on the 20th, agreed on the 20th, and in Bila on the 21st. So the results of these meetings secured this exchange to take place, of course under the auspices and with the help of the International Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the members of ECMM and the International Community who negotiated this deal, they would, of course, be the most knowledgeable people as to the facts and circumstances behind the causes of these kidnappings and also the reasons set forth for the release; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know which facts they had at their disposal, these international organisations, and how far they arrived at the right kind of knowledge, why these people were taken prisoner, were captured in the first place, and the circumstances governing the signing of the agreement and when it was decided that these two sides be exchanged, that both sides exchange prisoners according to the agreement reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, Brigadier, let us turn our attention to the actual combat orders that were issued on the 15th and also the morning of the 16th, and I'm talking about Exhibits 267, 268, and 269, Defence Exhibit 267, 268, and 269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's all right. Thank you, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There's nobody in the public gallery, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Are we in private session, Mr. President? (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: 6.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of October, 1998, at 11.00 a.m.
